note: Roll patterns are editable data, not code. Teachers vary slightly; the owner should confirm these against their own teaching material. Strings are 1..5 (1 = D4 top line in the tab renderer), fingers T/I/M. All notes are open-string eighth notes unless 'frets' gives a per-step fret (melodic/choker patterns). Optional fields: difficulty ('beginner'|'intermediate'|'advanced'), category, description.

rolls.title: Forward roll
rolls.description: The foundational Scruggs pattern: thumb on the low strings, index and middle alternating on the two high strings. The workhorse of most bluegrass breaks.

rolls.title: Backward roll
rolls.description: The mirror of the forward roll, starting on the first string. Useful for reversing direction mid-break and ending phrases on the thumb.

rolls.title: Forward-reverse roll
rolls.description: Rolls up over the fifth string and back down. The change of direction trips up beginners; practice slowly until the turnaround is even.

rolls.title: Alternating-thumb roll
rolls.description: The thumb alternates between the third and fifth strings, keeping the melody on the downbeats. Common when the melody sits on the low strings.

rolls.title: Up-down-the-neck roll
rolls.description: A scalar melodic run that climbs the first three strings and returns. Not a looping roll so much as an eight-note lick; keep all eight notes even.

rolls.title: Flank pick
rolls.description: Three notes played with the same finger (index here) followed by a thumb note, repeated. Great for syncopated melodic phrasing; try the version with the middle finger too.

rolls.title: Kimball roll
rolls.description: Don Kimball's signature lick: a quick ascending burst on the high strings landing on a low thumb note. The stretch from the high fret back to the open fifth string is the hard part.

rolls.title: Choked third (bend)
rolls.description: Bend the second string at the fourth fret up one whole tone (to the third-string pitch) while the roll continues underneath. Listen for the bent note matching the open first string's neighbor.

rolls.title: Choked fifth (bend)
rolls.description: A whole-tone bend on the short fifth string at the second fret, resolving back to open. Fifth-string bends need a firm grip and careful intonation check against the open third string.

rolls.title: Slurred ascent
rolls.description: A slide from the second to the fourth fret on the second string inside a forward roll. One pick per pair of notes; let the slide carry the second note.

rolls.title: Forward roll (Double C)
rolls.description: The same forward-roll fingering in Double C tuning. Old-timey clawhammer-style rolls feel different here; keep the thumb steady on the low C.

rolls.title: Backward roll (Sawmill)
rolls.description: The backward roll in Sawmill / G-modal tuning, where the lowered second string changes every chord shape you know.
